question: Will the haze in Singapore be better tomorrow?
later: Its number for today is checked as every answer's is; its forecast for tomorrow is kept with it, to check against tomorrow's measurements.
name: Claude
answer:
**It might improve a little, but don't count on it yet.** The most recent reports I found are from 16–17 October 2026, so check that "tomorrow" matches those dates.

- **Current situation:** Singapore is in its 13th consecutive day of unhealthy air since Oct 5, the longest stretch since the 2015 haze crisis. At 11am on Oct 17, the 24-hour PSI was in the "unhealthy" range in all regions. The readings were central 184, north 139, south 154, east 174 and west 176.
- **Reasons it could improve:** Winds are expected to gradually weaken and blow from the southeast or south. That could reduce the smoke drifting in from Kalimantan. Showers are also forecast over Singapore and parts of Kalimantan on Oct 18 and 19.
- **Reasons it might not:** Some smoke haze from Sumatra may still drift towards Singapore. The environment minister has also warned that the haze might reach hazardous levels, with PSI readings above 300, in the coming days because of weather conditions. The Star's headline says the haze should improve once the inter-monsoon period starts, but it doesn't say when.

**What to expect:** Conditions may ease slightly over the weekend if the winds shift and the showers arrive. The air will probably still be unhealthy, and it could get worse before it gets better.

**Checking tomorrow's air quality:** NEA issues a next-day PSI forecast each evening. Use the 24-hour PSI to plan the next day. Use the 1-hour PM2.5 reading for what you're about to do now. You can find both at nea.gov.sg.

**If you're going outside:** Elderly people, pregnant women and children should minimise outdoor activity when the forecast is "unhealthy" to "very unhealthy". People with chronic lung or heart disease should avoid outdoor activity.

# Singapore's PSI could go over 300 before haze improves once inter-monsoon period starts, says environment minister
The Republic has endured its longest stretch of poor air quality since 2015.

SINGAPORE (The Straits Times/ANN): The haze in Singapore might reach hazardous levels, with PSI readings exceeding 300, in the coming days due to weather conditions, said Minister for Sustainability and the Environment Grace Fu on Oct 16.

The Republic has endured its longest stretch of poor air quality since 2015 – Oct 16 marked the 12th consecutive day it registered unhealthy Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) readings.

Singapore last registered PSI readings above 300 in 2015, when it reached as high as 341.



The PSI has five bands: good (0-50), moderate (51-100), unhealthy (101-200), very unhealthy (201-300) and hazardous (>300).

As it is calculated across 24 hours, Fu said the reading is useful for assessing sustained exposure.

People should refer to the PSI in tandem with the other measurement of air quality, the hourly PM2.5 readings, she added.

Fu said a high 24-hour PSI reading and a low PM2.5 reading indicate that current conditions have improved, although prolonged exposure is still a concern.

Conversely, a low 24-hour PSI reading and a high PM2.5 measurement show that conditions have recently worsened, even though the longer-term average has not increased.

# Haze in Singapore: PSI back to ‘unhealthy’ range in all regions; PM2.5 enters ‘high’ range in the west
SINGAPORE – The hazy conditions continued in the morning of Oct 17 even as the 24-hour PSI in central Singapore dipped back to the "unhealthy" band after staying in the "very unhealthy" range the day before.

At 11am, the 24-hour PSI was in the "unhealthy" range in all regions: central (184), north (139), south (154), east (174), west (176).

Air quality is considered "unhealthy" when the PSI – a 24-hour rolling average of six key air pollutants – is in the range of 101 to 200, and "very unhealthy" when it is in the range of 201 to 300.



In its daily haze advisory on the evening of Oct 16, the National Environment Agency (NEA) said the PSI forecast for Oct 17 could be between 150 and 230, putting it in the range of "unhealthy" to "very unhealthy".

"With the winds forecast to shift to blow from the south-east or south-south-east, the transport of smoke haze from Kalimantan to Singapore may be reduced. However, some smoke haze from Sumatra may drift towards Singapore," the agency said.

Similarly, showers are also forecast over Singapore and parts of Kalimantan on Oct 18 and 19, it added.

“We can see that even with so few hot spots, with the right amount of wind and enough of this haze, smoke produced can give us very bad air for a (sustained) period,” he said Saturday on the sidelines of a community event in Tampines.



On Friday, air quality in Singapore hit unhealthy levels for the first time this year, as westerly winds brought smoke from forest fires in Sumatra to Singapore.
